items.title: 11 more bodies recovered from Upper Trishuli-1 tunnel
items.summary: Rasuwa, September 19 Eleven more bodies have been recovered from the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project site on Saturday. The Nepal Army said the bodies were found entangled in nets and buried under mud at the project site. According to the Army, all 11 bodies have been recovered and brought out of the area. items.summary: Prime Minister Balendra Shah is also expected to raise the issue of climate justice at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

items.title: Mud and steep cliffs hamper efforts to reopen flood-hit roads
items.summary: Twenty-four days after the Bhotekoshi floods, Rasuwa and Nuwakot remain cut off from each other, while Dhading district headquarters also lacks a direct road link.

items.title: Nepal begins probe into what triggered Bhotekoshi disaster
items.summary: A seven-member expert panel will trace the August 26 disaster from its source to downstream areas and examine geological, glacial and hydrological hazards, as well as the possible role of climate change.

items.title: Jumla waits for its young men who left to earn and never returned
items.summary: Forty-nine people from Jumla’s Patarasi Rural Municipality remain unaccounted for since the Bhotekoshi floods, including 15 young men from Lamri who had gone to Rasuwa for work.

items.title: 24 days after flood, hunger grips three Rasuwa wards
items.summary: Food is running out in villages cut off after the Bhotekoshi flood swept away bridges.

items.title: Six bodies recovered from Upper Trishuli-1 tunnel
items.summary: Rescue teams find the bodies of people missing since the August 26 Bhotekoshi floods as search continues inside the tunnel for possible further victims.
